inputs.share_count_basis: 88,249,856 issued less 514,439 treasury at 30 June 2026 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin); no dilutive securities (diluted EPS not stated for that reason). Held flat: SBC is nil, buybacks are episodic (JPY20.0bn Feb-2025 tender, cancelled FY2026) and treated as value-neutral.
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings only: 23,089 current + 7,119 non-current at 30 June 2026, less cash 130,290. Lease liabilities (~6.7bn, inside Other financial liabilities) EXCLUDED because leases are charged as an operating cost (treatment B).
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment line in any IFRS cash-flow statement FY2018-FY2026 nor in the J-GAAP years; SBC-zero market (treasury-share disposals of JPY270m in FY2026 are director compensation, immaterial). Treated as zero; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 'Interest and dividend income' per the cash-flow reconciliation (tanshin line 617), i.e. the income earned on cash and the cross-shareholding portfolio. Stripped because net cash (~100bn) is ~7x the FCF base and the portfolio is added back in the bridge (matching-asset rule).
inputs.last_fcf_note: owner FCF = reported FCF 19,557 - SBC 0 - interest & dividend income 3,639 - lease principal repayments 1,091 (financing, IFRS 16) = 14,827. The lease deduction is the treatment-(B) charge that the forward build carries as lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 (Mar-2026) purchases JPY7m. FY2025 carried the JPY20,018m tender buyback. Dividends are the primary return: JPY8,765m paid FY2026; FY2027 DPS guided JPY120 (~10.5bn).
inputs.fy0_note: FY2026 = year ended 31 March 2026 (repo end-year label; the company calls it FY2025). Year 1 of the projection is the year ending March 2027, which the company guides as FY2026.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built: 10y JGB ~1.7%, Japan ERP ~6.0%, beta ~1.05 for a net-cash specialty-materials name with a cyclical semiconductor segment -> cost of equity ~8.0%; negligible debt so WACC ~ cost of equity, 8.0%. Below the ~9% house reference for levered keiretsu auto suppliers because this company carries no net debt and a third of profit is defensive medical/packaging. Same rate in all three scenarios: cycle risk is in the flows and the weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: full lease payment (FY2026 principal 1,091 + interest ~100) charged inside EBITDA as lease_cost_pct_path 0.4% of revenue; lease liabilities excluded from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (14,257 total less ~1,100 ROU = ~13,150, 4.1% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; NCI stock of JPY3,328m (30 June 2026) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI profit share is ~1.2% of net income (352m FY2026) so the leakage is immaterial either way.
inputs.ebitda_basis: Business profit (revenue less COGS less SG&A, the company's headline) plus D&A, i.e. before 'other income/expenses' (impairments, restructuring, disposal gains). FY2026: 34,490 + 14,257 = 48,747 = 15.2% of revenue; FY2022-FY2025 ran 13.8-15.1%. Q1 FY2027 (Jun-2026) business profit margin was 14.3% (EBITDA ~18.9%).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year horizon (margin and capex paths still moving through year 5), scenario-weighted, per dcf-methods owner-fcf.md plus the non-US/cyclical adaptations. Chosen because this is an operating specialty-materials company (semiconductor encapsulation materials ~1/3 of revenue and ~half of business profit, high-performance plastics, medical devices and packaging films) with real free cash flow and a clean balance sheet. Kyocera chemical business acquisition (~JPY30bn, agreed Jan-2026, close targeted Oct-2026) is not in the June balance sheet: the consideration is deducted in the equity bridge and its revenue (assumed ~JPY20bn/yr; Kyocera does not disclose it separately) is layered into years 1-2 of every growth path (~5 months in FY2027, full year FY2028). Price is the 30-Oct-2026 TSE regular close; the H1 FY2027 (Sep-2026) results are due in early November and are the single event most likely to move year-1 drivers.

equity_bridge.item: Investment securities and other non-current financial assets at fair value
equity_bridge.note: Other financial assets (non-current) at 30 June 2026, Q1 FY2027 tanshin; predominantly FVOCI cross-shareholdings (FY2026 OCI gain 13,770 on this line). Added because their dividend income is stripped from the flows. Taken at balance-sheet fair value; the deferred tax on unrealised gains is not netted off, which overstates realisable value by up to ~30% of the embedded gain.
30 June 2026 balance sheet; flows are consolidated so NCI is charged once, here.

~JPY30bn cash consideration, agreed January 2026, targeted completion October 2026; not yet in the June 2026 balance sheet. Acquired revenue assumed ~JPY20bn/yr and included in the year 1-2 growth paths.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: between the 5-yr revenue CAGR (8.9%, flattered by the FY2022 post-COVID rebound and yen depreciation) and the 3-yr (3.9%); consistent with the Vision 2030 path (JPY420bn by FY2031 = ~5.6% CAGR from FY2026) plus the Kyocera addition
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 11.6% exceeds revenue 5-yr CAGR 8.9% by ~30% and lags EPS 5-yr CAGR 16.2% by ~28%: equity growth is inflated by FVOCI gains on cross-shareholdings (other components of equity 59.9bn -> 88.5bn in FY2026 alone) and EPS growth by the share count falling 6% on the FY2025 buyback and by FY2021 being a COVID-depressed base. Neither is a revenue signal; revenue and business profit are the anchors used.
historical_growth.eps_note: EPS CAGRs computed on total attributable net income (FY2021 13,198 -> FY2023 20,289 -> FY2026 28,014), not the per-share column, because of the 1-for-5 consolidation (2018) and 2-for-1 split (April 2024).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are on reported FCF less interest & dividend income less lease principal (FY2021 16,152; FY2023 5,274; FY2026 14,827). The 3-yr figure is off a working-capital-depressed FY2023 base and the 5-yr figure is negative because FY2021 was a COVID destocking year with unusually low working capital; neither is a trend. Reported FCF CAGRs are shown alongside for the record. Owner FCF has lagged business-profit growth because the FY2024-FY2026 capex programme (JPY50bn over the medium-term plan) and working-capital build absorbed much of the margin gain.

base.growth_note: Year 1 (Mar-2027): company guides +5.4% but Q1 ran +22.6% (semiconductor materials +40%, yen weaker); 13% = ~11% organic (H2 cooling from the Q1 run-rate) plus ~5 months of Kyocera. Year 2: ~5.5% organic plus the remaining ~7 months of Kyocera. Thereafter decelerating to 2% nominal; revenue reaches ~JPY448bn by FY2031 against the Vision 2030 target of 420bn organic plus ~20bn acquired.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Business profit + D&A. FY2026 15.2%, Q1 FY2027 18.9%. 17.0% in year 1 implies a business-profit margin of ~12.5%, above guidance (11.3%) but well below the Q1 print; held near 17% thereafter, consistent with the Vision 2030 business-profit margin target of 13% and a semiconductor segment that stays the mix driver without a cycle break.
base.capex_note: FY2026 4.8%, FY2025 5.1%, FY2024 7.6% (plan-year peak), FY2023 5.3%. The China +30% encapsulation expansion and the Suzhou/Singapore MUF lines (to FY2028) keep capex above D&A through year 4, converging to ~4.5% once the build-out ends.
base.cash_tax_note: FY2026 income taxes paid 10,280 on business profit 34,490 = 29.8%; income-tax expense 27.0% of pre-tax profit. Japan statutory ~30.6%; 29% blends the overseas mix.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer: receivables 64.2bn + inventories 68.6bn - payables 60.0bn = 72.7bn net working capital, ~23% of revenue, so growth consumes cash; -20% captures the FY2026 drag (OCF 35.0bn vs EBITDA-less-tax ~39.5bn on +15bn revenue).

scenario_narratives.base: The AI/power-device packaging cycle carries semiconductor materials through FY2028 but at a cooling rate: H2 FY2027 runs below the Q1 pace, the FY2027 guidance (revenue JPY337bn, business profit 38bn) is beaten but not by the Q1 annualised margin, and the Kyocera encapsulation business (~JPY30bn, ~20bn revenue) closes in October 2026 and is integrated without a profit hole. Group revenue reaches ~JPY448bn by FY2031, in line with Vision 2030 plus the acquisition, with the EBITDA margin settling at ~17% (business-profit margin ~12.5-13%, the Vision 2030 target) as the semiconductor mix offsets a structurally mediocre high-performance plastics segment. Capex stays above D&A through FY2030 for the China/Singapore capacity programme and working capital absorbs ~20% of each year's revenue gain. Terminal value is capped at 15x FCF (Gordon at 8%/2% would be 17x).
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI-server, HBM and power-semiconductor packaging supercycle persists for several years and Sumitomo Bakelite's ~40% share in epoxy molding compounds, the new MUF/compression-granule lines and the Kyocera assets convert it into revenue growth of 17%/12%/8% in FY2027-FY2029; semiconductor materials' business-profit margin holds above 20% (19.5% FY2026, 23.4% Q1 FY2027) and lifts the group EBITDA margin to 19-19.5%. The medical-device and pharma-packaging businesses keep compounding mid-single digits, high-performance plastics restructuring stops absorbing cash, and Vision 2030 (JPY420bn, 13% business-profit margin) is reached two years early. Terminal growth 2.5%, cap 15x.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2027 still finishes modestly ahead of guidance on the Q1 strength, but the AI-capex and memory cycle turns in FY2028: semiconductor materials volumes fall, Chinese domestic encapsulation suppliers and Resonac take share on price, the yen strengthens back toward 140 and reverses the translation tailwind, and North American automotive stays weak for high-performance plastics. Revenue falls 8% then 2% before recovering at 2-3%; the EBITDA margin drops to 13% (business profit ~9%, roughly FY2020-FY2021 levels) and recovers only to 14.5%. The Kyocera consideration is spent before its revenue is earned, and the capital programme runs through the downturn. Terminal growth 1.5% and a 13x cap reflect a company the market again treats as a cyclical chemicals supplier rather than an AI-materials compounder.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default: semiconductor materials is now about half of business profit, the Q1 FY2027 print (+51% business profit) sits at a demand level the company itself has not guided to, and a cycle turn plus yen reversal is a well-trodden path for this stock. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three things at once: the AI/power-device cycle lasting several more years, a group margin step-up to ~19.5% that the company has never delivered, and clean Kyocera integration. Base 50%: the balance sheet (JPY100bn net cash, no refinancing) and the defensive medical/packaging third mean the downside is earnings, not solvency.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on consolidated flows with no SBC (SBC-zero market), interest and dividend income stripped and the JPY100bn net cash plus the ~JPY52bn cross-shareholding portfolio added back in the bridge, leases charged as an operating cost, NCI and the pending JPY30bn Kyocera consideration deducted. The valuation is a judgment on how much of the Q1 FY2027 AI-driven step-up in semiconductor-materials demand is durable: the base case assumes the margin settles at ~17% EBITDA (vs 15.2% FY2026 and 18.9% in Q1), the bull assumes it is a new plateau, the bear assumes it is a cycle peak.
key_risks_to_valuation: Semiconductor cycle: half of business profit now comes from encapsulation materials, bonding pastes and substrates sold into AI servers, power devices and memory; a capex pause takes the group back to the FY2020-FY2021 margin band in the bear case

Guidance gap: FY2027 guidance (business profit 38bn) is far below the Q1 annualised rate (~54bn); the H1 results in early November 2026 will either upgrade and validate year 1 or confirm H2 normalisation
FX: ~64% overseas sales, yen weakness flattered FY2026 and Q1 FY2027; each JPY10 of yen strength against USD is a meaningful revenue and margin headwind
Kyocera chemical business integration (~JPY30bn, close Oct-2026): revenue and margin of the acquired business are assumed, not disclosed; deducted in the bridge at the full consideration
High-performance plastics has needed repeated North American impairments; the model's margin paths assume no further write-downs leak into cash
Cross-shareholdings taken at fair value in the bridge without netting the deferred tax on unrealised gains (~JPY590/share gross); a 30% haircut would remove ~JPY170/share
Terminal-cap dependence: the 15x cap binds in base and bull; the implied exit multiple on year-10 FCF is what a cyclical materials company has only intermittently commanded
